data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The safest deterministic reclamation protocol is an append-only intent-and-seal log with epoch fencing and monotonic-read witnesses; it dominates lease-based rivals because it records completion before reclamation can observe death, and the exact durable record must contain the ordered tuple (problem-id, content-addressed evidence-hash, seal-epoch, upstream-dependency-hashes, holder-intent-bit).","counterconditions":[{"case":"The log compaction or truncation removes seal entries before the reclaimer observes them.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Epoch counters wrap around or are reset during a partition, invalidating the fencing guarantee.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The reclaimer's log consumer is partitioned and has not yet observed the seal, causing indefinite workspace retention.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Before releasing the workspace, the holder appends a seal entry to a causally-ordered log. The reclaimer scans backward from the log tail for a seal entry matching the workspace problem-id; if none is visible in the reclaimer's causal cut, reclamation is forbidden. Epoch fencing prevents a zombie holder from sealing after the workspace has been reclaimed and reissued. The required durable record is therefore the seal entry itself plus the log's epoch-counter state at the time of sealing.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
